Woodside Shared Values
We take pride in who we are and in everything we do. Pride means setting high expectations for ourselves, valuing our achievements and taking responsibility for our actions. It encourages students to approach learning with confidence and to represent the school positively within the local community.
Kindness underpins how we support one another. We believe small actions make a real difference, whether through encouragement, listening or practical support. Kindness helps create a safe, welcoming environment where students and families feel valued and understood.
Respect shapes our relationships. We respect people for who they are and recognise the importance of fairness, inclusion and understanding. By valuing different backgrounds, experiences and viewpoints, we strengthen our community and prepare students for life beyond school.
Together, these shared values support our school mission: to provide exceptional education and experiences for every child, every day. They help create a culture where students feel confident to learn, grow and succeed.

Partnerships with colleges universities & businesses
Partnerships with colleges, universities, voluntary organisations and businesses
Our Careers education programme provides students with skills, knowledge, support and experience of the world of work to enable them to make informed career choices. Mulberry Academy Woodside has excellent links and partnerships with colleges, universities, voluntary organisations as well as businesses to create opportunities to inspire our students and widen their horizons.
We organise careers events and aspiration days throughout the year where many of our partners take part, as well as workshops and specific projects to enhance our students’ awareness of a wider range of career pathways.
Colleges and Sixth Forms
We have an extensive post-16 education programme throughout Years 10 and 11. We work with colleges and Sixth Forms and invite them in to Year 11 assemblies to share information. We also work with them to develop departmental links and organise subject specific events.
Universities
We work very closely with a number of different universities for specific projects:
Voluntary organisations
Our partnerships with voluntary organisations, such as IntoUniversity, The Girls’ Network, One Degree, Stemnet/Stem Ambassadors and Inspiring the Future, opens up opportunities to motivate and inspire our students about the world of work and challenges stereotypes.
Businesses
In order to raise the aspiration of our students and prepare them for their future work-life, we establish partnerships with both local, national, and international businesses.
We deliver work related learning to prepare our students for the world of work and help them to develop their employability skills through drop-down days and across the curriculum, working together with organisations such as Goldman Sachs and Marks and Spencer. We also work with businesses such as Nomura and RBS to deliver subject specific workshops as part of the IntoUniversity Initiative.
Partnership with LAET
We are proud to have a long-standing and highly effective partnership with the London Academy of Excellence Tottenham, a nationally recognised, academically selective sixth form with a strong track record of supporting students into top universities and competitive career pathways.
This partnership gives our students exceptional access to enrichment, academic stretch and futures opportunities from Year 7 through to Year 11, ensuring that aspiration, confidence and academic excellence are nurtured well before post-16 choices are made.
What This Partnership Means for Our Students
Through this relationship, selected students benefit from:
This is not a one-off collaboration, but a carefully structured, multi-year programme that grows with students as they progress through school.
A Programme That Starts Early and Builds Over Time
Key Stage 3 (Years 7–9)
Literacy and numeracy boosters to strengthen foundations
Key Stage 4 (Years 10–11)
As students move towards GCSEs, provision becomes increasingly focused on:
Widening Opportunity, Raising Aspiration
A core strength of this partnership is its shared commitment to widening participation. Students are selected not only on current attainment, but also on potential, curiosity and ambition.
For parents, this partnership provides reassurance that:
Many of our students who engage in this programme go on to successfully apply to selective sixth forms, including the London Academy of Excellence Tottenham, with the confidence and academic readiness to thrive.

Partnerships with charities
Basket Brigade UK
Basket Brigade UK is a loving, charitable organisation who deliver baskets of food, love and hope on December 23rd every year to those who could really do with a helping hand at Christmas.
Hundreds and hundreds of people (600-800) come together for one day and help create between 1000 -1500 baskets of food which they later deliver to those in need.
It’s a hard working but fun day and it is so rewarding to those who volunteer. At Mulberry Academy Woodside, We are super happy to announce that the venue for BB UK this year and the next five years is Mulberry Academy Woodside.
If you are interesed in volunteering, please visit the the resigration page by clicking this link.
Article : https://haringeycommunitypress.co.uk/2023/12/28/tottenham-volunteers-help-deliver-1000-christmas-food-hampers-around-london/
Hope in Haringey – African Schools Partnership
The Haringey African Schools Partnership bridges the interests of multiple schools and locations from across Haringey and Africa.
Through this initiative, White Hart Lane’s Mulberry Academy Woodsidew was paired with River State’s Okrika National School, Nigeria.
Throughout the school year, MAW helped raise money to help deliver two computers, a generator and a macbook to Okrika National School.
You can learn more about the Haringey African Schools Partnership by visiting their website – https://haringeyafricanschoolspartnership.com/
Mulberry Schools Foundation
Mulberry Schools Foundation is a charity set up in 2019 by Mulberry Schools Trust to support, develop and champion young people and their families in the Trust’s schools and partner schools and its local and global community.
Life chances, choice and wellbeing are underpinned by exceptional educational opportunity, unlimited by background; we seek to make this a reality for all children and young people.
Extending from the Mulberry Schools Trust community, we support, develop, champion, and create exceptional opportunities for children and young people facing disadvantage, so strengthening their capacity to make a difference in their world.

Partnerships with Primaries
Working with local primary schools has always been a key priority for Mulberry Academy Woodside. With recent changes to the National Curriculum, it is essential that students have a smooth transition from primary school to secondary school. This enables students to build on their prior skills and knowledge and ensures that there are ‘No wasted years’.
We hold taster days for Year 5 and Year 6 pupils to ensure that they feel comfortable with the surroundings and gain an idea of what to expect when moving up. The taster days offer taster sessions and the opportunity to meet other students. Our Year 10 peer coaches also work with these pupils to ensure that they feel at ease and confident with the transition.
Building Strong Primary Partnerships
We work closely with local primary schools to support pupils early and build confidence ahead of the move to secondary school. These partnerships reflect our commitment to inclusion, community and belonging. By working together, we help pupils feel welcomed, valued and supported long before transition begins. Strong relationships with primary staff and pupils allow us to understand individual needs and ensure continuity of care, learning and expectations. This early connection helps pupils arrive feeling secure, familiar and ready to thrive within a secondary school environment.
Enrichment, Culture and Celebration
Across the academic year, we deliver a planned programme of enrichment, performances and outreach that is inclusive, accessible and aligned with curriculum intent. This includes Black History Month performances, Festival of Arts, Winter Celebration Performance and Woodside on Tour, which brings pupil performances directly into primary schools. Spring term events include World Book Day, International Women’s Day, British Science Week, photography exhibitions and our annual Iftar event. These experiences celebrate diversity, promote equality and give primary pupils a positive and inspiring insight into secondary school life.
Transition, Leadership and Opportunity
As the summer term approaches, focus shifts to transition, leadership and confidence building. Staff and pupils deliver basketball coaching sessions in partner primaries and support sports days, modelling teamwork, responsibility and cooperation. Further opportunities include robotics workshops and curriculum taster days across English, maths, science, cooking and design technology. Science lessons remain a highlight, with interactive experiments that spark curiosity and enjoyment. Through this coherent programme of outreach and transition, pupils feel prepared, supported and confident as they move to the next stage of their education.
Learning in Tottenham (LIT)
Through LIT, staff collaborate with colleagues from partner primary schools to share ideas, reflect on practice and learn from one another. This includes joint projects, staff development opportunities and regular dialogue focused on curriculum, transition and pupil experience.
The partnership supports smoother transition from primary to secondary school, helping pupils feel confident and prepared for the next stage of their education. It also allows staff to build strong professional relationships rooted in a shared purpose and local understanding.
Working as part of the LIT group reinforces our belief that collaboration strengthens schools. By learning together and supporting one another, we help provide the best possible education for children across Tottenham.

Careers education information & guidance
At Mulberry Academy Woodside we are committed to ensuring that all our students in years 7 to 11 have high quality impartial advice on career opportunities, and that they progress onto appropriate courses or employment on leaving the school. It is very important to us to know that all leavers have a plan for their next step.
We support our students in making well-informed decisions by providing access to differentiated, impartial and independent information and guidance about the range of options (including academic, vocational, apprenticeships) that are most likely to help them to achieve their ambitions. We believe that giving students the best careers education and guidance is vital to improving their motivation to learn and help them to achieve.
If you have any questions regarding our careers education programme or you are a provider wishing to request access, please get in touch.

Provision is also monitored through regular feedback from students, parents/carers, staff, governors and our partners. Options Process
Introduction
Welcome to the options process for year 9 at Mulberry Academy Woodside, which will enable you and your child to select the subjects that they wish to study and are appropriate for them in Key Stage 4. This process has been designed to support us in achieving our aim to ensure all students leave school as highly qualified, confident and articulate young adults.
As you may be aware, all students have to stay in education or work-based training until the age of 18, so it is important that you and your child have time to think carefully about the subjects they would like to study in the next stage of their education as well as their future goals as these choices can have a direct impact on their Post 16 progression.
We hope the information below provides practical and straightforward advice that will support your child in choosing courses that suit their abilities and aspirations.
KS4 Curriculum Pathways
Our Mulberry Academy Woodside Key Stage 4 curriculum pathways provide the breadth and range of qualifications to prepare our students for a highly competitive, diverse and ever changing higher education system and employment market.
From year 10 we have split the curriculum into four pathways. All students will be allocated one of these pathways. This allows us to tailor a package of subjects that suits each child’s needs and abilities using attainment and progress data. This will give your child the best opportunity to succeed academically and will provide them with the widest range of educational and career opportunities when they leave school in Year 11.
The core curriculum
All students will study the ‘core’ compulsory national curriculum subjects.
Sciences
Religious Studies*
Non-examined subjects
In addition to this, all students will study a programme of PSHE and Physical Education. These are non-examined and will not lead to a qualification. Students who wish to study Physical Education in greater depth, may do so as one of their optional subjects.
The EBacc
Most of our students are expected to take a combination of subjects called the EBacc. The EBacc is a set of GCSE subjects that keeps young people’s options open for further study and future careers.
English language and literature
the sciences
geography or history
a language
The Separate Sciences
A group of students have been selected to study separate science in addition to EBacc. Students studying separate science at GCSE will cover more science content, so may be better prepared if they want to take science A-levels.
Facilitating Subjects
We believe that all students should follow an academically rigorous and appropriate pathway.
GCSE Religious Studies
The teaching of Religious Education is statutory. All students will continue to study this in KS4. All students will study a GCSE in Religious studies.
GCSE Computer Science
Students must be performing at least grade 4 in maths to take this subject.
Vocational
Students cannot choose 2 vocational courses to avoid an overload of internal assessments.
The Community Languages
Many students at Mulberry Academy Woodside can speak, read and write a second language, these are often referred to as community languages. We encourage students to develop language acquisition and provide some support and guidance for any student interested in being examined and gaining a GCSE in their chosen language. Please ensure that your child selects all languages that they can speak, read and write proficiently on the options form.
At Mulberry Academy Woodside, we believe it is important that all students are able to learn a new language in addition to those spoken at home as part of a broad and balanced curriculum. Therefore, taking a community language is an additional language and not in replacement for taking Spanish or French.

Where can I get my option form?

No, not at this stage. It is important to keep as many doors open as possible and to aim high! However, if you do have a serious career idea you should check if any subjects are essential or desirable.
Will I get all of my option choices?
The vast majority of students get their first or second choice, so it is highly likely they will get all of their choices.
Can I change my options in Year 10?
It is important to get your option choices right as changing can be very difficult, especially after you have missed some content of the course you may wish to change to.

Behaviour for Learning
At Mulberry Academy Woodside we strive to provide purposeful and stimulating environments for learning in which all students have the opportunity for success. Central to this are our shared values of pride, respect and kindness.
Shared Expectations
At Mulberry Academy Woodside, students are expected to:
Our staff team is committed to:
For our Four Pillars of Teaching and Learning, please visit our Teaching and Learning page.
Arrive prepared and ready to learn
Follow routines and instructions the first time
Contribute to a calm and positive environment
Modelling kindness, professionalism and calmness
Applying routines and expectations consistently
Building strong relationships with pupils and families
Teaching through the Four Pillars every day
Support excellent attendance and punctuality
Communicate promptly with the school when needed
Encourage positive behaviour and engagement in learning
Rewards and House Points
Students are recognised for their achievements in the following areas.
Scholarly behaviours will be rewarded and explicitly taught during assemblies and tutorial:
At Woodside we believe that rewards and celebration play a vital role in developing positive attitudes towards learning. Rewards are given in the ratio of three positives to one constructive criticism. Our praise point system allows students to be recognised for their achievements daily, weekly and throughout the year. Praise Points can be monitored by parents, carers and students through the classcharts app.
Students can earn praise badges for the number of praise points they accumulate across the year and will be awarded in assembly. Students who are awarded platinum badges will be invited on a reward trip and announced at House assemblies.
Bronze badge = 300 praise points
Silver badge = 500 praise points
Gold badge = 700 praise points
Platinum badge = 1000 points
Ready to learn
Ready to focus
Ready to think hard
Ready to reflect
Monitoring and Intervention
Mulberry Academy Woodside is committed to removing barriers for our young people. HOY and HODs will monitor the use of reward and sanctions for their department or year group with a member of the Leadership Team on a weekly basis. A comprehensive tracking system has been implemented to monitor interventions for students from Year 7 through to Year 11. Additionally, an interventions glossary has been developed for staff to facilitate precise and effective referrals, thereby optimising the support provided to each student. If students need additional support or intervention the following may be considered:
Interventions and Support
At Mulberry Academy Woodside we are inclusive in our approach and offer a wide range of interventions and support to ensure that students are able to manage their behaviour. These include:
Wellbeing Room;
Learning Mentors;
Positive reports and ‘on-track’ meetings;
Target setting and behaviour support plans;
1:1 literacy and numeracy intervention;
Respite placements at alternative provisions;
The Laurel
The Anchor Approach
The Anchor Approach
The Anchor Approach is the heart of our school culture. It underpins how we build relationships, respond to challenges and create a calm, predictable environment for learning.
The Anchor Approach ensures our school remains:
A safe harbour for every pupil
Sanctions: Conduct Points
It is imperative to delineate between minor infractions and more serious incidents (dangerous/abusive/high level), with sanctions tailored to the specific context of each case. Employing a restorative and child-centered methodology is paramount in addressing issues, aiming to preserve and enhance positive interpersonal relationships. Conduct points serve as a mechanism to alert students when their behaviour deviates from acceptable standards. This system, uniformly implemented throughout Mulberry Academy Woodside, provides students with the opportunity to reflect on their actions and change their behaviour.
Conduct points can be monitored by parents, carers and students through the ClassCharts app.
Positive reminder of behaviour
Verbal warning informing the student as to why this has been issued.
Conduct Behaviour (CB)
Conduct point for behaviour in lessons
If a student has received a positive reminder, a CB and continues to fail to meet the expectations of the school they will be collected from lessons by a member of staff (Student Support) and taken to the reflection room.
This is for the remainder of the lesson and 20 mins of their unstructured time.) A restorative will be completed with the class teacher and student. The removal from the lesson will also be communicated home by the class teacher.
If a student is involved in a more serious incident (dangerous/abusive/high level), they will be collected by student support and taken to the reflection room to write a statement and parent/carers informed. They will likely be out of circulation until the incident has been investigated.
Conduct Organisation (CO)
Conduct point for lack of organisation – equipment or uniform
Conduct Homework (CH)
Conduct point for incomplete homework, this may be escalated to a department or SLT detention.
